title: Init
summary: git init turns a folder into a repository, so git can start tracking it.

levels.title: Start a repository
levels.briefing: A repository is a folder that git is watching. git init creates a hidden .git folder where git will keep every version of your project. Nothing is saved yet: init only starts the tracking.
levels.objective: Turn this folder into a git repository.

cheatsheet.description: Make the current folder a repository
List files, including hidden ones like .git

hints: Right now git status says this is not a repository.
One git command creates a repository in the current folder.
levels.successMessage: The folder is now a repository. README.md shows up as untracked: git can see it, but nothing has been saved yet.

levels.title: From an empty folder
levels.objective: Create a repository in this empty folder, then create a file called notes.txt.
hints: Start the repository first, then make the file.
Run: git init, then touch notes.txt
levels.successMessage: A new file in a repository starts out untracked until you stage it.

levels.title: An existing project
levels.objective: This project has files but no repository. Make it a repository.
hints: Existing files are fine: git init does not change them.
Use the same command as before.
levels.successMessage: git init works in folders that already have files, and leaves them untouched.

levels.title: Init and add a file
levels.objective: Make this folder a repository and create an empty file called TODO.
hints: Two steps: start the repository, and create the file.
Run: git init, then touch TODO
levels.successMessage: The repository is ready, and git can see both files.
